title: Global and Climate-Zone-Based Correction of Landsat Water Surface Temperature in the TEAREE Model for Estimating Daily Lake Evaporation
content: Spatial estimates of reservoir evaporation from satellite observations are often inaccurate due to biases in raw satellite-derived water surface temperature (Ts_sat) and the need for concurrent in situ measurements of water surface temperature (Ts_m) for correction. This study expands the Turbulent Exchange Approach for Reservoir Evaporation Estimation (TEAREE) by developing transferable satellite-derived Ts_sat correction methods that eliminate the need for in situ Ts_m measurements at the application lakes. Analysis of 627 corresponding Ts_sat and Ts_m from 30 lakes across four climatic zones revealed climate-dependent biases, with a pooled mean bias of +1.53 °C and RMSE of 2.43 °C. Global (Method 1) and a climate-zone-based (Method 2) corrections were developed using 22 lakes and independently validated at eight lakes. Method 1 and Method 2 reduced satellite-derived Ts_sat RMSE from 2.92 °C to 2.15 °C and 1.87 °C, respectively. Incorporating these corrections into TEAREE reduced pooled daily evaporation RMSE from 1.37 mm/day to 0.81 mm/day (41%) and 0.62 mm/day (55%), respectively. Method 2 achieved comparable performance to the site-specific correction benchmark, with statistically equivalent mean evaporation estimates and absolute prediction errors at the pooled scale (TOST p < 0.001; ±5% equivalence margin). These findings demonstrate that climate-zone-based correction improves TEAREE evaporation estimates and supports broader application to lakes and reservoirs where in situ Ts_m measurements are unavailable.
